_what: DISCLOSED USEFUL LIVES, read from each company's OWN audited accounting-policies note. [R-TERM-01] requires the terminal's maintenance charge to rest on a DISCLOSED life and REFUSES one this desk chose (SIGCM clause 1), so the life has to be sourced before a terminal can be rebuilt — and until it is, the census can only say 'not sourced'. This file is where that research accumulates, one name at a time, so the next rebuild reads it instead of re-opening the filing.
_how: Every entry names the FILE, the NOTE and the ROUTE the figure came by (text layer or OCR off the rendered pixels), on the same footing as the four-field rule. A RANGE IS RECORDED AS A RANGE: most policy notes give a band per asset class and not a single number, and collapsing that to one figure here would be this desk choosing the life under cover of a citation. The weighted life a terminal actually needs is derived at rebuild from the property, plant and equipment note's own composition, which is a further sourcing step and is NOT done here.
_binds: Nothing reads this yet except the census's 'disclosed' column. A rebuild that uses one of these lives commits it to its own terminal_record, which is what the gate and the census then read [R-ENF-01].

ADNOCDIST.source: ADNOC Distribution, FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 3.10 (Summary of material accounting policies — property, plant and equipment): "Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line method to allocate their cost to their residual values over their estimated useful lives, as follows", printed page 23. The SAME table is printed a second time under note 4, Critical accounting judgments — 'Changes in Judgements', printed page 32, and the two agree class for class. Land was historically provided by the Government of Abu Dhabi and is carried at a nominal AED 1 per plot (note 3.10), so it is not depreciated; capital work in progress is not depreciated until commissioned (note 3.11).
ADNOCDIST.route: text layer via pdftotext -layout, CORROBORATED OFF THE RENDERED PIXELS at 200 dpi (pdftoppm, PDF page 25) and read as an image. THE PIXEL ROUTE IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: this table carries no arithmetic, so footing cannot arbitrate it, and a broken character map yields figures that look perfectly clean. The two routes agree character for character on all ten bands.
ADNOCDIST.SUPERSEDED_READING_the_register_was_a_ye: THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY READ 5-40 YEARS, CITED TO THE FY2024 AUDITED STATEMENTS, AND THE CENSUS PRINTED THAT FIGURE. It was not wrong about FY2024 — that filing carries a single column and it says 15-30 / 5-30 / 5-20 / 5-10 / 10-40, confirmed by opening it. It was stale, because the FY2025 audited statements sit in the same study directory and THE COMPANY REVISED THREE OF THE FIVE CLASSES UPWARD in them: buildings 15-30 to 15-50, furniture 5-10 to 4-15, pipelines 10-40 to 10-50. Plant and vehicles are unchanged. So the span is 4-50 on the current filing, not 5-40. THE FILING THAT MOVED THE LIVES IS THE FILING THAT QUANTIFIES THE MOVE — the same note carries the AED 90,917 thousand relief — so the staleness and the reason for it were one page apart, and the register cited the older one.
ADNOCDIST.prior_year_cross_check: RUN AND PASSED EXACTLY. The FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements' own policy note (engine/adnocdist_study/source_FY2024_audited_consolidated.pdf) gives 15-30 / 5-30 / 5-20 / 5-10 / 10-40, byte-identical to the 2024 comparative column printed beside the 2025 column in the FY2025 note. The prior filing therefore corroborates the comparative column, and the revision is real rather than a re-presentation.
ADNOCDIST.the_note_foots: PROPERTY, PLANT AND EQUIPMENT (note 5) WAS FOOTED CELL BY CELL AND PASSED WITH ZERO FAILURES ACROSS ROUGHLY FORTY TESTS, both years: every movement row sums across the six classes to its printed total (cost and accumulated depreciation); every class column rolls from opening through additions, transfers, disposals, impairment and exchange differences to its printed closing balance; closing cost less closing accumulated depreciation reproduces the printed net carrying amount for every class in both years; the FY2025 opening balances tie to the FY2024 closing balances class by class; and the note total ties to the balance-sheet line on a different page (AED 8,032,197 thousand and 7,552,178 thousand). ARITHMETIC IS THE ARBITER AND IT PASSED, so no OCR re-read of note 5 was required; one was done on the LIVES table anyway, for the reason in 'route'.
ADNOCDIST.weighted_not_derivable: THE WEIGHTED LIFE CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DISCLOSURE AND NO FIGURE IS CHOSEN INSTEAD. Unlike ADNOCLS and MODON the composition is NOT the obstacle — note 5 discloses cost, accumulated depreciation and net carrying amount for every one of the five depreciable classes, so a weighting is arithmetically available. WHAT IS MISSING IS A LIFE PER CLASS: the note discloses a RANGE per class, and weighting ranges returns a range. Weighted on the note's own gross cost the disclosed bands give 10.89 years at every low end and 39.87 at every high end — A SPREAD OF 29 YEARS; on net carrying amount 12.20 to 43.41. Buildings alone are 59.9% of gross cost on a band of 15 to 50, so the answer is decided almost entirely by where inside ONE class's range a figure is picked. That pick is this desk choosing a life under cover of a citation (SIGCM clause 1). THE IDENTITY ROUTE THAT WOULD COLLAPSE THE BAND IS CLOSED TWICE OVER AND THE ACCOUNTS SAY SO IN THEIR OWN WORDS. (i) RESIDUAL VALUES: note 3.10 allocates cost 'to their residual values', so the charge is (cost less residual) over life and gross cost over charge OVERSTATES the life by an unknown amount; no residual is disclosed. (ii) THE REASSESSMENT, QUANTIFIED BY THE COMPANY: AED 90,917 thousand of relief in FY2025 on assets carrying AED 5,347,053 thousand — 15.3% of the year's entire charge of 594,222, on 77.7% of the depreciable net book value, applied prospectively — so the FY2025 charge is not the charge that built the accumulated column above it and the identity is broken outright rather than merely biased. On the prior basis the implied life reads 20.51 years against 23.65 as reported and the measured age 10.47 against 12.07: a 15.3% swing in both from an accounting estimate rather than from anything about the assets. THE CHEAP CROSS-CHECK CANNOT ARBITRATE EITHER — the identity's 23.65 years sits inside the 10.89-39.87 band, but a band 29 years wide contains almost any number, so the agreement is worth nothing; the NOTE is the test and the arithmetic corroborates only sometimes. THE ALTERNATIVE BASIS WAS RUN AND IS ALSO CLOSED: 'disclosed_capex' needs a stated maintenance capital figure, and the FY2025 management discussion breaks capital expenditure down by PROJECT TYPE while putting new-station construction and capitalised property maintenance in the SAME category, saying only that 'about 50% of the CAPEX comprised development and construction of new service stations'; the H1 2026 management discussion says 'over 50% represented growth CAPEX' on AED 339 million, a bound over half a year rather than a figure. NEGATIVE SEARCHES ACTUALLY RUN, recorded so the next pass does not repeat them: no maintenance or sustaining capital figure appears in the FY2025 management discussion, the FY2025 or Q1/Q2 2026 results presentations, or the 2025 integrated report. So ADNOCDIST stays on the terminal ratchet WITH THIS REASON. Same disposition as ADNOCLS and MODON, reached by a different route: there the classes could not be split, here they can and the lives inside them are bands.
ADNOCDIST.what_would_open_it: THE RESIDUAL VALUES, in aggregate or by class — with those disclosed both identities work again on (cost less residual) and this name becomes straightforward. Or A PRE- AND POST-REASSESSMENT CHARGE BY CLASS, which the AED 90,917 thousand disclosure approaches but does not give: it names the carrying value affected and the total effect, not the split. Or A SINGLE LIFE PER CLASS rather than a band. None of the three is in the FY2025 audited statements, the FY2025 or H1 2026 management discussion, the FY2025 or Q1/Q2 2026 presentations, or the 2025 integrated report held in the study directory — that is a statement about what was searched.
ADNOCDIST.against_the_terminal: this study's terminal implies a replacement cycle of 66.7 years (1/g at g=1.5%) and charges 0.31x its own book depreciation — the lightest charge in the book. NOTHING THE COMPANY DISCLOSES LASTS BEYOND 50 YEARS even after the upward revision, and only buildings and pipelines reach it; the base the note itself turns over reads about 24 years on a broken identity. Per [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO] the defect runs the OPTIMISTIC way at a pegged 1.5% terminal, so correcting it would be EXPECTED to lower this value — expected, never predicted, because [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO CORRECTED] measures the sign per name and the first name actually rebuilt moved the other way. THE LIFE IS NOT THE ONLY BLOCKER: terminal_correction_price.py reports this name MISSING working_capital and ic_replacement as well, so no figure can be priced here even with a life, and the replacement-cost base needs an escalation from historical cost which needs an age — the same missing number again.

ADNOCLS.why_the_terminal_refused: MEASURED 04-Sep-2026, and it sharpens the earlier stop rather than repeating it. The rebuild computed maintenance as the WHOLE gross base at 25 years — 303,803 against book property depreciation of 385,487, i.e. 78.8% of it — so terminal free cash flow exceeded terminal profit and the module refused. THE 25-YEAR LIFE IS DISCLOSED FOR TANKERS, NOT FOR THE BASE. Applying one class's life to every class is the life-this-desk-chose error wearing a citation, and it is what produced the refusal.
ADNOCLS.what_the_disclosure_does_support: The gross cost IS disclosed by class and every class has its own disclosed life, so only the vessel line mixes two — hulls at 25 years and dry-docking components at 5 — and only that line is unsplit. The other four classes are 315,131 of 7,595,070 (4.1%), and their depreciation is bounded by their own disclosed ranges to between 23,993 (longest lives) and 61,785 (shortest). Subtracting from the 385,487 the company reports across notes 5 and 6 leaves the vessel line depreciating 323,702 to 361,494, and solving (V-x)/25 + x/5 for that BOUNDS THE DRY-DOCKING COMPONENT TO 2.79%-6.04% OF THE VESSEL LINE. That is arithmetic on the disclosure, not a choice.
ADNOCLS.the_next_step_is_named: Maintenance at the disclosed lives on the GROSS base equals book depreciation on that base by construction, straight-line — which is why the honest charge is near 385,487 rather than 303,803, and why the refusal reverses at any point inside the bound above. WHAT REMAINS is the step from historical to CURRENT cost, and the gap there is NARROWER THAN THIS ENTRY FIRST SAID — see the correction below.
ADNOCLS.exemplar_note: This is the model report [R-ENF-01 EXTENDED 04-Sep], so its terminal is inherited by every study built by opening it. Its terminal currently sits 7.5% BELOW its own NOPAT floor, and the correction indicated above RAISES it — which is stated here because L-289 forbids reading the direction off the census, and because a correction moving an exemplar's value up is exactly the kind nobody chases.
ADNOCLS.CORRECTION_the_price_input_is_partly_hel: AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS ENTRY SAID BROKER-QUOTED VESSEL PRICES ARE NOT HELD AND NAMED THEM AS THE MISSING INPUT. That was written after reading four years of filings and the impairment note, and WITHOUT READING THE STUDY'S OWN INPUT REGISTER, where two observed vessel prices already sit: a 2017-built very large crude carrier SOLD in January 2026 for USD 111.0mn against a carrying value of USD 83.0mn (vessel_sale_price / vessel_sale_book, from the FY2025 earnings release), and ELEVEN VESSELS ACQUIRED for about USD 1.3bn announced 7 August 2026 (acq_2026_cost — six very large crude carriers and five gas carriers, two of them newbuildings). Both are transacted prices, not quotes. [R-IND-01]'s own lesson, landing on the desk that was about to escalate: the ladder says OPEN THE ARTEFACT, and the register is an artefact this search skipped.
ADNOCLS.what_is_actually_still_missing: The fleet composition IS held by class — owned tankers HS 2, MR 16, LR1 9, LR2 17, VLCC 8 at FY2026 — so a capacity-times-price base is constructible in shape, the same shape ARCC and Fertiglobe use. WHAT IS NOT HELD is a per-class replacement price for the classes other than the very large crude carrier: MR, LR1, LR2 and handysize, plus the gas and offshore fleets. The sale price is a NINE-YEAR-OLD ship's secondhand value and the acquisition is a blend across two classes with two newbuildings inside it, so neither is a newbuild price per class and neither may be spread across the fleet. THAT is the gap, and it is one research step rather than an absent market.

ADNOCLS.CORRECTION_05-09-2026_the_band_was_under: THIS ENTRY CARRIED THE SIX VESSEL CLASSES AND NOT THE OTHER FOUR, so it read 2-40 years and the census printed that. The FY2025 policy note discloses TEN classes and its widest is BUILDINGS, PORTS, WHARVES AND LAND IMPROVEMENTS AT 7-50 YEARS, so the disclosed band is 2-50. The four added classes are 4.15% of depreciable gross cost and do not move a weighting; the point is that a partial transcription of a policy note reads exactly like a complete one, which is why the route and the class list are recorded rather than the band alone. Re-read off the rendered pixels of FS_FY2025.pdf page 33 as well as the text layer.
ADNOCLS.CORRECTION_05-09-2026_the_dry_docking_bo: 'what_the_disclosure_does_support' bounds the dry-docking component to 2.79%-6.04% of the vessel line by solving (V-x)/25 + x/5 against the residual charge. THAT ARITHMETIC REPRODUCES EXACTLY (23,993 / 61,785 / 323,702 / 361,494 all to the digit) AND ITS BOUND IS A PROPERTY OF THE 25 IN IT, NOT OF THE DISCLOSURE. The note puts SIX lives in that one column - dry docking 2-5, offshore 20-25, tankers 25, dry-bulk and containers 25, gas carriers 25-40, jack-up barges 40 - so the solve is ONE EQUATION IN FIVE UNKNOWN CLASS COSTS. Re-run at other hull composites the same residual charge gives 4.95-8.12% at 27.5 years, 6.68-9.79% at 30, 9.27-12.30% at 35 and 11.12-14.09% at 40: a five-fold move driven entirely by the assumed hull life. The company's OWN FY2022 and FY2023 notes disclose the vessel line as a single band, 'Vessels (excluding dry docking component) 20 - 40 years', which contradicts 25 outright; the FY2024 note is where it was disaggregated into five classes and no carrying amount followed the disaggregation.

fleet_age_route_run_05-09-2026.why: TERMINAL_EVIDENCE named a disclosed average fleet age as one of three things that would open this terminal, and said it was worth one look before being called closed.
fleet_age_route_run_05-09-2026.found: ADNOC L&S investor presentation April 2026, appendix slide 22, 'Owned Shipping Fleet (as of 31 December 2025)': owned counts and average age by vessel type, 87 vessels. Footed - 53+20+11+3=87 against the stated blocks and total. Read off the rendered pixels because the text layer's block assignment does not foot (it puts FSU with the tankers, giving 55 and 18 against a stated 53 and 20); the pixels put FSU in the gas block and every subtotal then foots.
why_it_does_not_open_it: IT IS COUNTS AND AGES, NOT CARRYING AMOUNTS. Weighting by vessel count is not weighting by value and the two are far apart on this fleet - a very large crude carrier contracts near USD 136mn against an MR near USD 45mn on this file's own verified newbuild prices, so a count weight silently prices a VLCC and an MR the same.

ONE AGE IS NOT DISCLOSED AT ALL: LNG, 8 of the 87 owned vessels, prints as 'XX' in the published deck - an unfilled placeholder, and the newest and among the most valuable part of the fleet. The 79 vessels that do carry an age count-weight to 9.87 years; the 8 that do not are exactly the ones that would move it.
A VESSEL AGE IS NOT THE CHARGE-WEIGHTED AGE OF THE DEPRECIABLE BASE the escalation identity needs, which also carries buildings, ports, plant, equipment and the capitalised dry-docking components.
fleet_age_route_run_05-09-2026.so: Route 3 is RUN and CLOSED. Assembling a life or an age out of a count-weighted, incomplete table is the life-this-desk-chose error in a third costume, and the direction is not even safe: the missing 8 are the youngest.

ADNOCLS.weighted_life_05-09-2026: REFUSED. The weighting [R-TERM-01] needs is by the property, plant and equipment note's own carrying amounts, and note 11 carries SIX columns - buildings, VESSELS AND MARINE EQUIPMENT, plant, equipment and vehicles, furniture, and capital work in progress. 97.85% of depreciable net book value (95.85% of depreciable gross cost) sits in the single vessels-and-marine-equipment column, which spans six disclosed lives from 2 to 40 years and is disclosed at no finer level in any of the four years of statements, either annual report, the investor presentations or the management discussion. THE NOTE DISCLOSES THE LIVES AND IT DOES NOT DISCLOSE THE COMPOSITION THEY WOULD BE WEIGHTED BY. Any single figure is this desk choosing one, so none is recorded. What the accounts DO give, and it is a bound rather than a life: the vessel column's charge-implied composite is 20.14-22.49 years and the whole depreciable base's cost-over-charge is 19.70 years - both OVERSTATEMENTS, because this note depreciates to residual values and reassesses vessel salvage annually, so the charge is (cost - residual)/life and cost/charge exceeds the life.

AIRARABIA.cross_check: THE TABLE PRINTS ITS OWN COMPARATIVE COLUMN — 2025 beside 2024 — and every class is identical in both, which is the cross-check inside one document. The FY2024 statements committed beside it carry no text layer (65 bytes) and were not needed.
AIRARABIA.an_apparent_contradiction_resolved: The FY2025 policy note opens 'During the year, the Group changed the estimated useful life applied to certain assets ... refer Note 5', while the table it introduces shows NO change between 2025 and 2024. Note 5 settles it: the reassessment was 'during the year ended 31 December 2024', effective 1 October 2024 — aircraft lives raised from 15 to 20 years, residual values cut from 20% to 7-8% of original cost, quantified at AED 29.3mn on net assets and AED 26.7mn on net profit. THE OPENING SENTENCE IS PRIOR-YEAR PROSE CARRIED FORWARD IN THE COMPANY'S OWN FILING. It is recorded because a reader who stopped at that sentence would date a change to the wrong year, and because a disclosure that contradicts its own table is the shape this house is supposed to notice — it is theirs and not ours, and the resolution is theirs too.
AIRARABIA.why_this_name_matters_here: AIRARABIA is one of the seven terminals charging LESS than their own book depreciation and one of the three doing it while sitting more than 10% BELOW the price. Its retired terminal implies a replacement cycle of 1/g = 40 years against a DISCLOSED aircraft life of 20 — it charges roughly half the maintenance the disclosure implies, on the asset class that carries essentially all the value. Correcting it moves the value DOWN and therefore AWAY from the price, which is [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO]'s point and the side of the correction this house has never measured.
AIRARABIA.not_yet_collapsed: A RANGE IS RECORDED AS A RANGE, though this one is unusually well determined: an airline's value sits in aircraft and engines, both disclosed at a single 20 years rather than a band. The weighting is still a further sourcing step, and the 7-8% residual belongs in it — maintenance at replacement cost over 20 years against a 7-8% residual is not the same charge as over 15 against 20%.

BOROUGE.route: FOUR READS, THREE OF THEM INDEPENDENT OF EACH OTHER. (1) text layer, pdftotext -layout, which carries the Years column; (2) text layer, pdftotext without -layout, which carries it too - the inverse of the AMR case, where -layout was the one that dropped it; (3) OCR OFF THE RENDERED PIXELS, pdftoppm -r 200 on PDF page 28 read as an image, which is the arbiter because a column of lives has no arithmetic to foot against; (4) the FY2024 filing, a separate document with its own Producer string, by text layer and by pixels. All four agree.
BOROUGE.the_note_foots: note 6 was footed cell by cell in both years and in all three directions against its printed totals - every movement row ACROSS to the Total column, every class column DOWN from opening to printed closing, and the identity cost less accumulated equals net book - plus the FY2025 opening row against the FY2024 filing's own printed closing row, and the year's charge against its allocation note (408,732 + 36,611 + 4,040 + 1 = 449,384). 78 tests, NO BREAK. So the text layer is arbitrated by arithmetic on the figures, and by pixels on the lives, which carry none.
BOROUGE.prior_year_cross_check: FY2024 and FY2023 filings both disclose Buildings 15-40, Motor vehicles 4-10 and Furniture 3-4 IDENTICALLY, and Plant and machinery at 8-30. Three filings, three documents, three years: the only figure that moved is the top of the plant-and-machinery range, 30 to 35, which is the FY2025 reassessment the note describes. THE CHANGE IS DISCLOSED AT BOTH ENDS - a decrease in the charge of USD 90,335 thousand in 2025 and an expected USD 179,198 thousand in 2026 - and the note says lives rose "by up to an additional 10 years" while the class range top rose 5, which is a tension the note does not resolve and this entry does not resolve either.

weighted_life_band.method: carrying-amount-weighted HARMONIC mean on note 6's own columns, capital work in progress excluded. maintenance = sum(IC_c / L_c) and terminal_value.build() charges IC_total / L, so the single life reproducing that charge is IC_total divided by that sum. An arithmetic mean would overstate the life and undercharge. This is an identity, not a choice.
weighted_life_band.stability: the band barely moves across weight base or year. Its WIDTH is not a weighting artefact - it is plant and machinery's own disclosed 8-to-35 range carrying 93.9% of the base.

BOROUGE.not_yet_collapsed: THE CLASSES WEIGHT AND THE BAND DOES NOT COLLAPSE. The note discloses the split, so the weighting is available and is arithmetic; what it returns is 8.16 to 34.19 years, a factor of 4.2. Picking a point inside that is this desk choosing the life under cover of a citation, which [R-TERM-01] refuses outright (SIGCM clause 1). THE SPREAD IS NOT ACADEMIC: priced through terminal_value.build() on the study's own FY2030 figures, two of the four base-by-endpoint constructions REFUSE and the two that build straddle the published terminal from -12.9% to +16.3%, on a terminal holding 76.7% of enterprise value.
BOROUGE.the_measured_age_route_stays_closed: [L-328] conditions (i) and (ii) are both evidenced in the same note, and (ii) is quantified at both ends. Depreciation writes off "cost less estimated residual values"; and a life reassessed from 1 July 2025 means the FY2025 charge is half a year on the old lives and half on the new, so accumulated depreciation over that charge is nine years of one basis divided by half a year of another. The same accumulated balance supports 14.98 years (pre-change), 17.99 (as reported) and about 22.42 (go-forward) with nothing about the assets having moved. Not a measurement.
BOROUGE.against_the_terminal: this study's terminal carries the retired reinvestment identity: a replacement cycle of 50.0 years, which is 1/g at a pegged 2.0% terminal to the decimal, charging 16.7% of terminal profit. FIFTY YEARS IS A FACT ABOUT THE DIRHAM'S PEG, AND THE DISCLOSED LIVES DO NOT REACH IT ANYWHERE - the longest life the company discloses for any class is 40 years, for buildings, which are 5.7% of the depreciable base, and the weighted band tops out at 34.19. So the terminal assumes a life longer than the accounts support, in the direction that OVERSTATES value - and the priced range still spans both signs, because the band is too wide to settle it.
BOROUGE.what_would_open_it: (a) a narrower disclosure for plant and machinery, which is 93.9% of the base and whose own 8-to-35 range is the entire width of the band; (b) the residual values, in aggregate or by class, which would reopen the identity route; (c) the FY2026 charge as reported, the first full year on the new lives, which lands the go-forward denominator on the same basis as the accumulated column - a date rather than a hope; (d) a replacement-cost capital base at the terminal year, which this study does not commit and which the pricing above had to bracket with a net-book floor and a historical-cost ceiling.

DU.not_yet_collapsed: THE CLASSES WEIGHT AND THE BAND DOES NOT COLLAPSE — 3.00 to 23.93 years, a factor of 8.0. Picking a point inside it is this desk choosing the life under cover of a citation, which [R-TERM-01] refuses outright (SIGCM clause 1). THE SPREAD IS NOT ACADEMIC: priced through terminal_value.build() on this study's OWN committed terminal inputs, changing nothing but the life, the terminal runs 91,494 at the low end and 76,524 at the high end against a committed 82,050 — +11.5% to -6.7%, an 18-point span. AND THE SIGN OF A CORRECTION DEPENDS ON THE MAINTENANCE BASIS, WHICH IS WHY NOBODY MAY PREDICT IT: under 'book_dna_escalated', which is what this study commits because it holds no replacement-cost capital base, the life enters only through the escalator (1+pi)^(L/2), so a SHORTER life means a SMALLER charge and a HIGHER value; under 'disclosed_life', IC_replacement/L, a shorter life means a LARGER charge and a LOWER value. The two bases run in opposite directions on the same life, and the ratio in the census column arbitrates neither. Nothing published is moved by this entry.
DU.the_measured_age_route_stays_closed: [R-TERM-01] condition (i) is evidenced in the note's own words and then reinforced: depreciation allocates cost 'NET OF THEIR RESIDUAL VALUES', and the critical-estimates note 2.2(iv) says residual values are actively estimated — 'the Group uses historical sales and management's best estimate based on market prices of similar items'. So the charge is (cost - residual)/life rather than cost/life, and BOTH identity routes are biased UPWARD by the same mechanism: accumulated/charge (12.61 years) is not this base's age, and gross cost/charge OVERSTATES the life. This is the SAVOLA shape exactly — the arithmetic cross-check cannot catch it here because the disclosed band (3.00-23.93) contains the identity's answer trivially, so THE NOTE IS THE TEST AND THE ARITHMETIC IS SILENT. Conditions (ii) reassessment and (iii) business combination are both clean: no change-in-estimate language anywhere in the FY2025 filing, and no acquisition line in any of the three roll-forwards.
DU.against_the_terminal: this study has ALREADY been rebuilt through terminal_value.py and commits a life of 16.6997 years, so the census reads that and not this band. THAT COMMITTED LIFE IS DERIVED, NOT DISCLOSED, and its own record says so: gross depreciable cost over the year's own charge, per note — PP&E (29,737,447 - 1,121,091 CWIP)/1,542,393 = 18.55, intangibles (4,071,746 - 571,459)/239,907 = 14.59, right-of-use 3,726,888/364,063 = 10.24, blended 16.6997, cross-checking to 15.9586 on FY2024's own columns. Every one of those reproduces exactly from the notes read here. The route's own self-validation also stands: the right-of-use component derives 10.24 years against the 10.1 years note 7 STATES as the average lease term, 1.4% apart. What this entry adds is the half the derivation could not supply — the DISCLOSED lives are a band 3.00 to 23.93 years wide, the committed 16.70 sits inside it and is therefore not contradicted by it, and the residual-value clause means the derived figure is an UPPER BOUND on the true life rather than a measurement of it. An overstated life understates maintenance under a replacement-cost basis, and DU's committed central of AED 16.5778 already sits 45.9% ABOVE the spot it was struck at — but the direction a rebuild would take is NOT predictable from that, because this study's terminal stands on 'book_dna_escalated' where a shorter life REDUCES the charge. The under-charging ratio is a flag, not an inference [R-TERM-01 clause two corrected]: the sign is measured per name, at a rebuild, and not before one.
DU.what_would_open_it: (a) a carrying amount for any of the six plant-and-equipment sub-classes the FY2024 filing names — the lives are disclosed and only the weights are missing, so one disclosure closes it; (b) the residual values, in aggregate or by class, which would reopen both identity routes and convert the derived 18.55 into a measurement; (c) a narrower plant-and-equipment band in a later filing, that class being 98.9% of the base; (d) a replacement-cost capital base at the terminal year, which this study does not commit and which is why its terminal stands on 'book_dna_escalated' rather than 'disclosed_life'.

ELEC.the_identity_route_is_closed_and_the_fil: THE USUAL FALLBACK — depreciable gross cost over the year's own charge — FAILS ITS OWN PRECONDITION HERE, and the note discloses the reason on the same page. 'تكلفة الأصول المهلكة دفتريا بالكامل وما زالت تعمل' (cost of assets fully depreciated in the books and STILL IN USE) is EGP 93,877,527, which is 27.3% of the EGP 343,770,105 depreciable gross cost and 32.9% of machinery. Those assets carry no charge, so the denominator is not cost/life. MEASURED ON THE ONE CLASS THAT CAN FALSIFY IT: computers are disclosed as a single 5 years, and cost/charge returns 19.50 — 3.90x the disclosed life. Excluding the fully-depreciated cost gives 17.54 years overall and reproduces the bands well (computers 5.47 against 5, furniture 10.00 against 5-10), but that construction assumes the 27.3% that is fully written down AND STILL RUNNING never needs replacing, which is the opposite of what the disclosure says. The two constructions the same note supports differ by 38% (24.13 against 17.54 years) and the note does not choose between them. For scale, terminal_value.py's own re-pointing note records EGCH at 1.3% fully depreciated, where the proxy was usable; this is twenty-one times that.

weighted_life_derived.identity: depreciable cost / the year's depreciation charge
weighted_life_derived.source: Fertiglobe plc, 2025 Annual Report, note 7 property, plant and equipment — the cost and accumulated-depreciation table at 31 December 2025, and the 'Depreciation and impairment' movement row for the year.
weighted_life_derived.why_derived_and_not_chosen: THE DISCLOSED BANDS CANNOT BE COLLAPSED WITHOUT CHOOSING. Buildings 10-50, plant and equipment 5-30, fixtures 3-10: any single figure taken from those is this desk picking a life, which [R-TERM-01] refuses outright. What the note ALSO discloses is the composition at COST and the year's charge, and their ratio is an IDENTITY rather than an assumption — the composite life the company's own accounts are actually running. It is LABELLED derived, on the same footing as capex derived by dPPE + D&A and EGCH's years derived from disclosed rates.
weighted_life_derived.the_impairment_caveat_and_why_it_does_no: The movement row is labelled 'Depreciation and impairment', so in a year carrying an impairment the ratio would understate the life. This report states at note 12 that 'no impairments were required for the year ended 31 December 2025', so the row is pure depreciation and the identity is exact. IN A YEAR WITH AN IMPAIRMENT THIS DERIVATION WOULD NOT BE AVAILABLE, and that is a property of the disclosure rather than of the method.
weighted_life_derived.coherence_check: The derived 22.04 years sits INSIDE the disclosed plant-and-equipment band of 5-30, and plant and equipment is 94.6% of the depreciable cost base — so the figure the arithmetic produces and the class that dominates the base agree. That is the check that makes a derived life usable rather than merely arithmetic.
weighted_life_derived.against_the_retired_terminal: The retired terminal charges g x IC, so it implies a replacement cycle of 1/g = 50.0 years at this study's 2% terminal — 2.27 TIMES the life this company's own accounts depreciate its assets over. That is the [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO] direction reversal measured on one name with its own numbers: in a pegged market the identity does not starve the asset base, it flatters it, and correcting it moves the value DOWN.

classes.note: the lower of the lease term or 10 years, so the short end is the lease

MODON.source: Modon Holding PSC FY2025 consolidated financial statements, property, plant and equipment accounting policy: 'The estimated useful lives for the current and the comparative periods are as follows', followed by the table. Land is not depreciated.
MODON.weighted_not_derivable: THE WEIGHTED LIFE CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DISCLOSURE AND NO FIGURE IS CHOSEN INSTEAD. Two of the note's own columns each combine assets whose disclosed lives differ by an order of magnitude, and neither can be split from anything the filings publish. (1) LAND AND BUILDINGS ARE ONE COLUMN — AED 12,438,392 thousand, 73% of the gross cost — and LAND IS NOT DEPRECIATED AT ALL while buildings run 2 to 50 years, so the depreciable base inside the largest class is unknown. (2) PLANT (40 years) shares a column with MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT (3 to 4 years), a more than tenfold spread on AED 883,217 thousand. THE CHARGE-IMPLIED ROUTE IS ALSO CLOSED and for a reason worth recording: FY2025 carried AED 832,492 thousand of assets acquired through business combinations, most of it into the plant column, so a full-year charge over an average base measures the timing of an acquisition rather than a life — the implied figures come out at 20.7 years on a class disclosed at 3 to 4, and 12.4 years on one disclosed at 2 to 5. Neither route is a disclosure and A LIFE THIS DESK CHOSE IS NOT A DISCLOSED LIFE (SIGCM clause 8), so MODON stays on the terminal ratchet WITH THIS REASON rather than being conformed on an invented number. Same disposition as ADNOCLS, for the same kind of gap.
MODON.against_the_terminal: this study's terminal is BELOW ITS OWN NO-GROWTH FLOOR — the worst symptom the retired reinvestment identity produces, and the one that says the construction is charging more for growth than the growth is worth. Its implied replacement cycle is 1/g = 40.0 years, which happens to equal the disclosed life of PLANT alone while the rest of the base runs 2 to 5 years. Correcting it is worth at least +6.2% (3.54 -> 3.76 at the floor) and cannot be done until the weighted life can be sourced.

PHAR.source: EIPICO (PHAR) FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements, note 3.1 'Fixed assets and depreciation': 'The depreciable fixed asset value ... is depreciated according to the straight-line method over the estimated useful life of each type of fixed asset ... (land is not depreciated)', followed by the table of estimated lives. EVERY LIFE IS A SINGLE FIGURE, not a band, which is unusual in this file and makes the weighting unambiguous.
PHAR.verified_independently: RE-SOURCED FROM THE FILINGS AND CONFIRMED. The gross-cost-weighted harmonic mean of the disclosed class lives computes to 13.7954 years (depreciable gross cost 2,701,916,171 over a weighted annual charge of 195,855,726), reproducing the 13.8 committed. Priced through terminal_value.py at the exact figure the terminal moves +0.0074% on frame A and +0.0058% on frame B — immaterial. RATES ADD AND LIVES DO NOT: weighting the LIVES arithmetically instead gives 20.7158 years, 50.2% too long. Weighting on NET BOOK VALUE rather than gross cost gives 15.1535, 9.8% longer, and is NOT adopted — net book value measures how much of an asset has been consumed rather than the rate at which it is consumed, and because the short-lived classes here are the most depreciated (transportation 89% written down) it lengthens the life and under-charges maintenance. Full working in engine/phar_study/useful_lives.json.
PHAR.route_verified: The text layer is FAITHFUL but the note DOES NOT FOOT in three places, so both property, plant and equipment pages were re-read by OCR off the rendered pixels (pdftoppm -r 300 -gray, pdf pages 27 and 28) and the pixels confirm the text layer figure for figure, including the failing cells. (i) note 4.1 transportation accumulated depreciation rolls to 95,515,215 against a stated 95,515,206, out by +9, and (ii) the same nine reappears in the disposals row, 957,912 against 957,921 — the defective cell is the disposals figure, where 57,465 rather than 57,456 makes both foot, a transposition. (iii) note 4.2 states accumulated depreciation at 31/12/2023 of 1,645,282,556 against columns summing to 1,645,282,546, confirmed three ways as the +10 error: the columns, the FY2024 note's own 1/1/2024 opening balance, and the FY2023 STANDALONE filing whose note 4 foots with zero failures. ALL THREE SIT IN ACCUMULATED DEPRECIATION; every COST row foots in both filings and ties 31/12/2023 to 1/1/2024 exactly, and cost is the only base the weighting reads.
PHAR.prior_year_cross_check: The FY2023 composition, agreeing class by class between the FY2024 comparative and the FY2023 standalone filing, weights to 14.2840 years on an IDENTICAL table of disclosed lives — so no life was reassessed between the two years. The 3.5% shortening into FY2024 is pure mix: additions of 89.2mn machines, 44.3mn tools and 42.6mn furniture against 0.6mn of buildings.
PHAR.measured_age_refused: THE MEASURED-AGE ROUTE IS RULED OUT BY THE COMPANY'S OWN POLICY NOTE. Note 3.1 depreciates 'the cost of the asset minus its residual value' — condition (i) in terminal_value.py, the SAVOLA and EMPOWER condition — so accumulated depreciation over the year's charge OVERSTATES the age and may not be read off the accounts. Here, unlike SAVOLA, the arithmetic corroborates the note rather than waving it through: the identity-implied life (2,701,916,171 / 95,547,071) is 28.28 years against the 13.7954 the class rates weight to, +105% apart. The declined age is 18.21 years against a half-life of 6.90; at the house 7% terminal that would move the escalator from 1.5947 to 3.4282, maintenance from EGP 722.0mn to 1,551.9mn, and the terminal DOWN 55.0% on frame A and 43.1% on frame B. Conditions (ii) and (iii) do not bite — no life reassessed, no business combination in the cost roll-forward.
PHAR.census_reads_this_band_and_should_not: PHAR HAS ALREADY BEEN REBUILT THROUGH terminal_value.py AND COMMITS 13.8, yet the census still prints 'sourced 5-50 yrs' for it. The reason is a resolver blind spot, not a gap in the study: terminal_census.disclosed_life() looks for terminal_record at the TOP LEVEL of study_numbers.json, and PHAR is a two-sided study whose terminals are committed per frame at dcf.frame_A.terminal_record and dcf.frame_B.terminal_record. This is the ARCC false negative that resolver's own docstring records, closed for the flat case and still open one level down for any two-sided study. Reported, not fixed here — a change to what a gate reports is its own decision.
PHAR.weighted_from: the gross cost by class in note 4.1 at 31-Dec-2024 — buildings 543,426,318 at 50 years, machines and equipment 1,701,915,589 at 15, transportation 107,581,637 at 5, tools 151,105,707 at 5, furniture 197,886,920 at 10 — on a depreciable base of EGP 2,701,916,171 which foots to the note's stated 2,785,102,203 once land of 83,186,032 is excluded. The rates add, not the lives, so the weighted life is the reciprocal of the weighted annual rate.
PHAR.against_the_terminal: this study's terminal implies a replacement cycle of 20.0 years (1/g at g=5.0%) against a disclosed weighted life of 13.80 — it charges maintenance over a life 45% longer than the accounts run, which UNDER-charges. THE DIRECTION IS SET BY THE TYPED GROWTH RATE AND NOT BY THE MARKET: [R-TERM-01 CLAUSE TWO] reasons from a terminal at zero real growth, where 1/g is the reciprocal of inflation and runs SHORT in a high-inflation economy. This study typed 5% nominal in a 7%-inflation economy — a real DECLINE — so its 1/g runs long in exactly the market the clause says it should run short. At the house terminal of 7% the implied cycle would be 14.3 years, close to the disclosed 13.80, which is a coincidence of magnitudes rather than a law and is recorded as one.
